A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same persona-based emotional-support study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the new Appendix H in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4–6 report original persona-trait measurements, dialogue simulations, ablations, and human evaluations. The appendices contain additional correlation and persona-consistency results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and human evaluations and adds descriptive results comparing generated dialogue lengths in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The persona-extraction, HEXACO/CSI assessment, dialogue-generation, and persona-reassessment procedures are unchanged. The corresponding prompts in Appendices A, B, and D are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use ESConv, CAMS, Dreaddit, and PersonaHub for the same trait-measurement and emotional-support tasks. Appendix H examines the existing with/without-persona conditions without introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Haiku, and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct. The persona/no-persona and HEXACO/CSI comparisons are unchanged; newly cited methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds supplementary measures of dialogue length: word totals, turn counts, and mean words per turn, including separate seeker/supporter measurements. Existing generation settings, the 1,000-persona PersonaHub sample, and the 10-annotator/50-group human-evaluation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix H analyzes how persona inclusion affects dialogue length and turn structure. The persona-injection ablation in Section 5.3, HEXACO-versus-CSI strategy comparison, and qualitative case study are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The correlation significance reporting, including the p-value statement in v1 Table 2a and v2 Table 2, is unchanged. No new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures appear; Table 16 provides descriptive counts and means.

E6.justification: New Table 16 reports 10,398 versus 12,666 total turns and 21.01 versus 18.37 words per turn, with versus without personas. Existing correlation coefficients, strategy percentages, trait-distribution plots, and human ratings are unchanged, including the overall 39% win, 27% tie, and 34% loss result.

T1.justification: The psychological inventory definitions, assumed relationships between dimensions, and correlation-based reasoning are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, research questions, and conclusions retain the same claims about inferring persona traits, emotionality/extraversion shifts, and persona-dependent support strategies and empathy. The conclusion's wording edits do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 replaces part of the empathy-building explanation for self-disclosure with a caution about poorly bounded self-disclosing chatbots. Appendix H newly links fewer turns and longer utterances to targeted questioning and conversational efficiency. The existing limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 specifies approximately 20 USD per hour for annotators, replacing v1's unspecified standard hourly wage. This is additional study documentation, not evidence of changed compensation or a rerun. Model identifiers, temperature, and supplied prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on proactive and mixed-initiative dialogue, chatbot self-disclosure, and persuasion, including Deng et al., Meng and Dai (2021), and Petty and Cacioppo (2012). It also repairs missing Zheng et al. (2024) attribution. These additions expand supporting context without redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and typo corrections, revises the author/contact header, adds acknowledgments, and appends the dialogue-statistics section. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Existing table panels receive standalone table numbers and revised captions, several figures and tables move, and Table 16 is added. The underlying visual designs remain largely unchanged; Figure 1 also corrects a label typo.

improvement.justification: Appendix H adds useful quantitative description absent from v1, while repaired citations and explicit annotator compensation improve clarity and traceability. The gains are limited: the principal experimental evidence is unchanged, and word/turn statistics alone do not establish the new interpretation of greater conversational efficiency and depth.
